sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Sarah and David Reza recently bought a place outside of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 莎拉和戴维·雷扎最近在华盛顿特区外买了一处房产。

sentences.en: They sound excited because this is the first time they're hosting both their families.
sentences.zh: 他们听起来很兴奋，因为这是他们第一次同时招待双方的家人。

sentences.en: We are making today a vegetable frittata with tomato, basil, and goat cheese.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要做的是西红柿、罗勒和山羊奶酪蔬菜烘蛋。

sentences.en: We've got home fries.
sentences.zh: 我们准备了家常炸薯块。

sentences.en: We've got regular waffles.
sentences.zh: 我们还有普通华夫饼。

sentences.en: Sarah and David wanted to start a new tradition.
sentences.zh: 莎拉和戴维想开启一项新传统。

sentences.en: Cook brunch with ingredients from their home garden.
sentences.zh: 用自家花园里的食材做早午餐。

sentences.en: The home fries have rosemary from our garden and the frittata has basil from our garden.
sentences.zh: 炸薯块里用了我们花园里的迷迭香，烘蛋里用了我们花园里的罗勒。

sentences.en: This is Sarah's way of going back to her family's roots.
sentences.zh: 这是莎拉回归家庭根源的方式。

sentences.en: She remembers her mother doing the very same thing.
sentences.zh: 她记得她母亲也做过同样的事情。

sentences.en: I remember growing up, my mom had a garden,
sentences.zh: 我记得我小时候，我妈妈有一个花园，

sentences.en: and she would always come back with these tiny little tomatoes and be like,
sentences.zh: 她总是会带回这些小小的西红柿，然后说，

sentences.en: I provided for my family.
sentences.zh: 我养活了我的家人。

sentences.en: Look, family, I grew this.
sentences.zh: 看，家人们，这是我种的。

sentences.en: And we're like, yeah, that's the smallest tomato ever.
sentences.zh: 而我们当时想的是，天哪，这是有史以来最小的西红柿。

sentences.en: But there's something about being able to grow stuff
sentences.zh: 但能够种植一些东西，

sentences.en: and being able to give it to people that you love that's pretty exciting.
sentences.zh: 并能把它送给你爱的人，这种感觉真的很棒。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: My grandmother would always say that...
sentences.zh: 我祖母总是说……

sentences.en: This is Sarah's brother, Zach.
sentences.zh: 这是莎拉的弟弟，扎克。

sentences.en: The sharing food is important, but I'd say the most important part is being around the table.
sentences.zh: 分享食物很重要，但我认为最重要的是围坐在桌子旁。

sentences.en: But food was the lure to get everyone done.
sentences.zh: 但食物是把大家聚在一起的诱饵。

sentences.en: Food, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 食物，没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: Food kept us there.
sentences.zh: 食物让我们留在了那里。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Food brought us together.
sentences.zh: 食物把我们聚在了一起。

sentences.en: But it's the company and the conversation.
sentences.zh: 但陪伴和交谈才是最重要的。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, the profound role that food plays in our lives.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将探讨食物在我们生活中所扮演的深远角色。

sentences.en: Food is not just nutrition that goes in your mouth or even pleasant sensations that go with it.
sentences.zh: 食物不仅仅是进入你口中的营养，甚至也不仅仅是随之而来的愉悦感。

sentences.en: It connects to your whole life.
sentences.zh: 它与你的整个人生息息相关。

sentences.en: We look at the culture and psychology that determine what we eat,
sentences.zh: 我们研究决定我们吃什么的文化和心理，

sentences.en: what we spit out, and when we come back for more.
sentences.zh: 我们吐出什么，以及我们何时会再来一份。

sentences.en: Paul Rasen has been studying the psychology and culture of food for more than 40 years.
sentences.zh: 保罗·拉森研究食物的心理学和文化已经超过40年了。

sentences.en: He works at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他在宾夕法尼亚大学工作。

sentences.en: Early in his career, Paul found himself pondering a question that few of us might think to ask.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯早期，保罗发现自己正在思考一个我们很少有人会去问的问题。

sentences.en: Why do so many people across the world enjoy the hot, stinging pain of chili peppers?
sentences.zh: 为什么全世界有那么多人喜欢辣椒那种火辣、刺痛的感觉？

sentences.en: This question took Paul to a small village in Mexico
sentences.zh: 这个问题把保罗带到了墨西哥的一个小村庄，

sentences.en: where chili peppers were as common as salt and pepper in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在那里，辣椒就像美国的盐和胡椒一样普遍。

sentences.en: They don't think their food tastes good without it.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得没有辣椒，食物就不好吃。

sentences.en: And the little kids don't like it.
sentences.zh: 而小孩子并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: So something happens somewhere between two and five years of age.
sentences.zh: 所以，在两到五岁之间发生了某种变化。

sentences.en: At the meals where everybody adult is eating the hot pepper and the older children are,
sentences.zh: 在餐桌上，所有的成年人都在吃辣椒，大一点的孩子也在吃，

sentences.en: and they're all enjoying it, and the little kid is thinking it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 他们都吃得很开心，而小孩子却觉得这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And after a while, some magic occurs, and the little kids like it.
sentences.zh: 过了一段时间，某种魔法发生了，小孩子们也喜欢上了它。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, there are a number of possible accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，嗯，有几种可能的解释。

sentences.en: Some accounts involve something fundamentally biological.
sentences.zh: 有些解释涉及一些根本性的生物学因素。

sentences.en: And presumably the biological explanation would be if you start eating it long enough,
sentences.zh: 据推测，生物学上的解释是，如果你吃得足够久，

sentences.en: you're eventually just going to like it for biological reasons.
sentences.zh: 你最终会因为生物学原因而喜欢上它。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: The brain compensates for all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 大脑会补偿各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: We adapt to things.
sentences.zh: 我们适应事物。

sentences.en: This is a case of more than adaptation where you're turning something that's negative into something positive.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是适应，你把负面的东西变成了正面的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, that's an amazing thing, that we can start with something that's innately negative
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，这是一件了不起的事情，我们可以从天生负面的东西开始，

sentences.en: and make it really positive.
sentences.zh: 并把它变得非常积极。

sentences.en: So I said, let's take a look at the animals in the village,
sentences.zh: 所以我说，让我们看看村里的动物，

sentences.en: because the dogs and the pigs eat Mexican food.
sentences.zh: 因为狗和猪也吃墨西哥食物。

sentences.en: They're eating tacos and hot sauce and beans and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 它们吃塔可饼、辣酱、豆子等等。

sentences.en: So I went around the village, and I first asked people,
sentences.zh: 所以我走遍了村子，首先问人们，

sentences.en: do you have any dogs or pigs that like hot pepper?
sentences.zh: 你们有没有喜欢吃辣椒的狗或猪？

sentences.en: And they said, what, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 他们说，什么，你疯了吗？

sentences.en: I said, well, yeah, I mean, they eat it.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，我是说，它们确实吃啊。

sentences.en: And they said, that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 他们说，那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I said, would you mind if I give the dogs a little piece of cracker
sentences.zh: 我说，如果我给狗一块饼干，

sentences.en: with some hot sauce on it and without and see what they choose?
sentences.zh: 上面涂点辣酱，另一块不涂，看看它们选哪个，你们介意吗？

sentences.en: So they said, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 他们说，请便。

sentences.en: And so I did go around the village with pigs and dogs.
sentences.zh: 于是我带着猪和狗在村子里做了实验。

sentences.en: I put one cracker in front of them with hot pepper sauce and another without,
sentences.zh: 我把一块涂了辣椒酱的饼干和一块没涂的放在它们面前，

sentences.en: and I'd see what they did.
sentences.zh: 看看它们会怎么做。

sentences.en: And it turns out that none of them ate the hot pepper firSt.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，它们没有一个先吃辣椒味的。

sentences.en: They all ate the one with hot pepper because they're hungry,
sentences.zh: 它们都吃了带辣椒的那块，因为它们饿了，

sentences.en: but their first choice was the one without hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 但它们的首选是不带辣椒的那块。

sentences.en: So that I couldn't find an animal in the village that did what everyone over five years old
sentences.zh: 所以我无法在村里找到一种动物能像五岁以上的人类那样，

sentences.en: and humans did, which was to gobble this stuff out and prefer it.
sentences.zh: 狼吞虎咽地吃下这些东西并偏爱它。

sentences.en: So that suggested to me that it seems to be uniquely human.
sentences.zh: 这向我表明，这似乎是人类独有的。

sentences.en: And so this is not just a question of people getting used to it and getting to like it,
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是人们习惯并喜欢上它的问题，

sentences.en: because the dogs and pigs are eating the garbage.
sentences.zh: 因为狗和猪也在吃垃圾。

sentences.en: The garbage is laced with chili peppers.
sentences.zh: 垃圾里混杂着辣椒。

sentences.en: If that was the case, that would be true for the animals as well.
sentences.zh: 如果真是那样的话，这对动物来说也应该适用。

sentences.en: So what was happening in the humans, in the human brain, if you will,
sentences.zh: 那么人类身上，或者说人类大脑里发生了什么，

sentences.en: that allowed five-year-old children to fall in love with chili peppers
sentences.zh: 让五岁的孩子爱上了辣椒，

sentences.en: and kept their canine cousins from liking it?
sentences.zh: 却让它们的犬科表亲不喜欢它呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's indeed exactly the question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实就是问题所在。

sentences.en: We don't know how this happens, but we do know that where it happens is at the meals,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这是怎么发生的，但我们确实知道它发生在餐桌上，

sentences.en: where the kids are eating with their parents and their older siblings,
sentences.zh: 孩子们和父母以及大一点的兄弟姐妹一起吃饭，

sentences.en: and they keep eating it because there's social pressure to eat it.
sentences.zh: 他们继续吃是因为有社交压力。

sentences.en: Now, the animals keep eating it too because they're hungry.
sentences.zh: 现在，动物们也继续吃，因为它们饿了。

sentences.en: So it can't be just that they keep eating it.
sentences.zh: 所以不能仅仅因为它们一直在吃。

sentences.en: So it's really, to me, a miracle.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这真是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: And what I realized is that it's a miracle that takes place in humans all over the world,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，这是一个在世界各地人类身上发生的奇迹，

sentences.en: not just about hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是关于辣椒。

sentences.en: It's also about liking coffee, which is bitter,
sentences.zh: 这也关于喜欢咖啡，咖啡是苦的，

sentences.en: and people don't like it originally, and they like it.
sentences.zh: 人们起初不喜欢，后来却喜欢上了。

sentences.en: And it goes outside the food domain.
sentences.zh: 而且这超出了食物领域。

sentences.en: People like to go on roller coasters.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢坐过山车。

sentences.en: Now, a roller coaster is a very negative experience the first time you have it, right?
sentences.zh: 坐过山车第一次体验时是非常负面的经历，对吧？

sentences.en: You think you're crashing to death, and your heart is pounding,
sentences.zh: 你以为你要坠毁身亡了，心脏狂跳，

sentences.en: and yet people pay to do this.
sentences.zh: 然而人们却花钱去玩这个。

sentences.en: Can you imagine a dog paying to go on a roller coaster?
sentences.zh: 你能想象一只狗花钱去坐过山车吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it just won't happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这根本不可能发生。

sentences.en: So we found that there's a whole range of things in which humans enjoy what is originally negative,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，人类享受一系列原本负面的事物，

sentences.en: and they come to enjoy it as positive.
sentences.zh: 并最终将其视为积极的体验。

sentences.en: This includes the fatigue of running.
sentences.zh: 这包括跑步的疲劳感。

sentences.en: It includes sad movies.
sentences.zh: 包括悲伤的电影。

sentences.en: It includes being afraid in horror movies.
sentences.zh: 包括在恐怖电影中感到恐惧。

sentences.en: This seems to be only humans.
sentences.zh: 这似乎只有人类才会这样。

sentences.en: So our thought, and it's only a thought,
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法，仅仅是一个想法，

sentences.en: is that what humans are enjoying is the very fact that their body thinks that something is bad,
sentences.zh: 是人类享受的正是他们的身体认为某事很糟糕，

sentences.en: but they know it's okay.
sentences.zh: 但他们知道这没关系的事实。

sentences.en: We call it benign masochism.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为良性受虐。

sentences.en: Humans have this special ability to appreciate the fact that they know that something that their body is saying is bad is actually good.
sentences.zh: 人类有一种特殊的能力，能够欣赏这样一个事实：他们知道身体所说的“糟糕”其实是“好的”。

sentences.en: And we have evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我们有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, for chili pepper, the favorite degree of hotness is just below the level of unbearable pain.
sentences.zh: 例如，对于辣椒，最受欢迎的辣度刚好低于难以忍受的疼痛水平。

sentences.en: They're pushing as far as they can to get their body to really scream,
sentences.zh: 他们尽可能地推向极限，让身体真正尖叫着说，

sentences.en: get this out of here, and yet know that it's okay.
sentences.zh: 把它弄出去，但同时又知道这没关系。

sentences.en: So it seems to be a very general feature of humans,
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是人类的一个非常普遍的特征，

sentences.en: which we tapped into by asking why a couple of billion people like hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 我们通过询问为什么几十亿人喜欢辣椒来挖掘这一点。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the theory is that you start out not liking it,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，理论是这样的：你开始时不喜欢它，

sentences.en: and then social pressure, if you will, convinces you to try it,
sentences.zh: 然后社交压力（如果你愿意这么说的话）说服你去尝试，

sentences.en: and then you try it often enough that your body learns to adapt to it a little bit,
sentences.zh: 然后你尝试的次数足够多，你的身体学会了一点点适应它，

sentences.en: but then eventually you start to like it for actually a slightly different reason.
sentences.zh: 但最终你开始喜欢它，其实是因为一个稍微不同的原因。

sentences.en: You're no longer liking it just because of the peer pressure or the social interactions.
sentences.zh: 你不再仅仅因为同伴压力或社交互动而喜欢它。

sentences.en: You're liking it because it gives you a sense that you're coming close to the edge of something thrilling.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢它是因为它让你感觉到自己正在接近某种令人兴奋的边缘。

sentences.en: Is that the argument?
sentences.zh: 这就是你的论点吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there's something thrilling that is not threatening.
sentences.zh: 是的，有一种令人兴奋但并不具有威胁性的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, for example, if something is threatening, you don't get to like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，如果某事具有威胁性，你就不会喜欢它。

sentences.en: Like people don't get to like serious pain.
sentences.zh: 就像人们不会喜欢严重的疼痛一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It has to have something of the sense of it's not really threatening.
sentences.zh: 它必须带有一种“它并不是真的具有威胁性”的感觉。

sentences.en: And it even becomes funny.
sentences.zh: 它甚至变得很有趣。

sentences.en: So in the case of disgust, people don't like disgusting things, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在厌恶的情况下，人们不喜欢令人作呕的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: But they make exceptions.
sentences.zh: 但他们会破例。

sentences.en: They eat smelly cheese, and they come to like that smell in the context of the cheese,
sentences.zh: 他们吃臭奶酪，并且在奶酪的背景下喜欢上了那种气味，

sentences.en: even though their body is saying, get this out of your mouth, it stinks.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们的身体在说，把它从嘴里弄出来，它太臭了。

sentences.en: You once performed an experiment on yourself.
sentences.zh: 你曾经在自己身上做过一个实验。

sentences.en: You were with your wife, I believe, at a Korean restaurant in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我相信当时你和你的妻子在纽约市的一家韩国餐厅。

sentences.en: And you did an interview with NPR back in 2015 where you told the reporter that it was one of the hottest things you'd ever eaten.
sentences.zh: 你在2015年接受NPR采访时告诉记者，那是你吃过的最辣的东西之一。

sentences.en: Tell me that story.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲那个故事。

sentences.en: Well, my wife at the time was a cookbook writer, and she was very interested in cuisine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时的妻子是一位食谱作家，她对烹饪非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And we went to a Korean restaurant in New York.
sentences.zh: 我们去了纽约的一家韩国餐厅。

sentences.en: And the people around us, they were ordering some dish that we didn't recognize.
sentences.zh: 周围的人都在点一些我们不认识的菜。

sentences.en: So we said to the waiter, we would like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对服务员说，我们想要那个。

sentences.en: And he says, you don't want that.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们不会想吃那个的。

sentences.en: I said, no, no.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，不。

sentences.en: We said, we'd really like to try new foods.
sentences.zh: 我们说，我们真的很想尝试新食物。

sentences.en: He says, you don't want to try that food.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们不会想尝试那种食物的。

sentences.en: So this went on, and we won, of course.
sentences.zh: 事情就这样继续下去，当然，我们赢了。

sentences.en: And he brought this dish, and it was unbearably hot.
sentences.zh: 他端来了一道菜，辣得让人受不了。

sentences.en: And we ate it because we were shamed into eating it by our own insistence that it was good.
sentences.zh: 我们还是把它吃光了，因为我们之前一直坚持说这菜很好吃，为了面子只能硬着头皮吃下去。

sentences.en: I have another story of a different sort.
sentences.zh: 我还有另一个不同类型的故事。

sentences.en: It also happened in New York.
sentences.zh: 它也发生在纽约。

sentences.en: I had a colleague who had a dog, and the dog liked to eat dog poop.
sentences.zh: 我有个同事养了条狗，那条狗喜欢吃狗屎。

sentences.en: So they would go into Washington Square Park with the dog, and the dog would just hunt out a dog poop and eat it.
sentences.zh: 他们会带狗去华盛顿广场公园，狗就会在那儿到处找狗屎吃。

sentences.en: And it was just awful.
sentences.zh: 这简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, they hated it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们对此深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: The dog smelled it.
sentences.zh: 狗闻了闻它。

sentences.en: So they went to a vet, and the vet said, why don't you put hot pepper on the dog poop?
sentences.zh: 于是他们去看兽医，兽医建议说，为什么不在狗屎上撒点辣椒粉呢？

sentences.en: Because dogs don't like hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 因为狗不喜欢辣椒的味道。

sentences.en: So they go into Washington Square.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了华盛顿广场。

sentences.en: I want you to get this image.
sentences.zh: 我想让你想象一下这个画面。

sentences.en: Barbara's holding the dog on a leash, and her husband goes with a shaker of hot pepper,
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉牵着狗，她丈夫拿着一瓶辣椒粉走过去，

sentences.en: finds a dog turd, and seasons it in front of everybody with all this hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 找到一坨狗屎，当着所有人的面，在上面撒满了辣椒粉。

sentences.en: And I mean, the idea of someone seasoning a dog turd is really pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有人给狗屎调味这种想法，真的挺绝的。

sentences.en: And then they let the dog go, and the dog ate it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们松开狗，结果那条狗还是把它吃了。

sentences.en: And did the dog stop eating dog poop?
sentences.zh: 那条狗停止吃狗屎了吗？

sentences.en: No, no, because the dog liked dog poop more than it disliked the hotness.
sentences.zh: 没有，因为比起讨厌辣椒的辣味，它更喜欢吃狗屎。

sentences.en: You know, people will put up with pain to do something they really like, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们为了做自己真正喜欢的事，是可以忍受痛苦的，对吧？

sentences.en: Just as Paul has shown that the sense of taste is shaped by the brain,
sentences.zh: 正如保罗所展示的那样，味觉是由大脑塑造的，

sentences.en: he's also done work that shows the same thing for appetite.
sentences.zh: 他还做过研究，证明食欲也是如此。

sentences.en: In one study, he sat a meal down before patients who had amnesia.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，他给患有健忘症的病人端上一顿饭。

sentences.en: The general view in most of the people who work on hunger is that hunger comes when,
sentences.zh: 大多数研究饥饿感的人普遍认为，饥饿感产生于，

sentences.en: you know, your body reserves are low, maybe your blood glucose is low, various hormones
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你的身体储备不足时，也许是血糖偏低，各种激素

sentences.en: come out, and you feel this sensation of hunger, and you eat until it disappears.
sentences.zh: 分泌出来，你就会感到饥饿，然后一直吃到这种感觉消失为止。

sentences.en: Now, there's some truth in that, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这其中确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: But there are many other higher order things.
sentences.zh: 但还有许多其他更高层面的因素。

sentences.en: So, for example, the cultural definition of what's a meal is very important.
sentences.zh: 例如，对“什么是正餐”的文化定义就非常重要。

sentences.en: After you finish the meal and have dessert, you stop eating.
sentences.zh: 吃完正餐再吃点甜点，你就会停止进食。

sentences.en: So, to try to show this, we dealt with the two amnesic patients who were totally amnesic.
sentences.zh: 为了证明这一点，我们找了两位完全失忆的健忘症患者进行实验。

sentences.en: They didn't remember anything that happened more than 30 seconds ago.
sentences.zh: 他们记不住任何超过30秒前发生的事情。

sentences.en: But they were quite intact otherwise.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，他们的其他功能都很正常。

sentences.en: So, we fed them lunch in a situation where they were in a room without a clock.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们在一个没有时钟的房间里给他们提供午餐。

sentences.en: And we said, lunchtime, and it was lunchtime, and we brought them a favorite lunch of theirs.
sentences.zh: 我们说，午餐时间到了，确实也是午餐时间，我们给他们端上了他们最爱吃的午餐。

sentences.en: We'd ask them what their lunch was, and they, of course, ate it.
sentences.zh: 我们问他们午餐吃什么，他们当然吃掉了。

sentences.en: Then we took the plate away.
sentences.zh: 然后我们收走了盘子。

sentences.en: There were no more signs that they'd eaten.
sentences.zh: 没有任何迹象表明他们刚刚吃过饭。

sentences.en: And 10 minutes later, we brought another lunch and said, lunchtime.
sentences.zh: 10分钟后，我们又端来另一份午餐，说，午餐时间到了。

sentences.en: And they all ate it three times each, the second lunch completely.
sentences.zh: 结果他们每人都吃了三次，第二份午餐也完全吃光了。

sentences.en: Then we took that away, waited 10 minutes, and brought a third lunch.
sentences.zh: 然后我们收走盘子，等了10分钟，又端上了第三份午餐。

sentences.en: Each of these were full-size lunches.
sentences.zh: 每一份都是足量的午餐。

sentences.en: And most of the time, they ate the third lunch.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，他们还是把第三份午餐吃完了。

sentences.en: Twice, I think, one of them said, I'm getting a little stuffed,
sentences.zh: 我想其中一个人有两次说，我有点撑了，

sentences.en: meaning their stomach was really getting full.
sentences.zh: 意思是他们的胃确实已经饱了。

sentences.en: But the point was that they're eating, when you're served a meal, it's, and if it looks palatable, you tend to eat it.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，当有人给你端上一顿饭，如果看起来很可口，你往往就会吃下去。

sentences.en: I was on a plane once flying to Chicago, and at three in the afternoon, they served a full lunch.
sentences.zh: 有一次我坐飞机去芝加哥，下午三点的时候，他们供应了一顿完整的午餐。

sentences.en: Now, everyone had eaten lunch already.
sentences.zh: 当时每个人都已经吃过午饭了。

sentences.en: But six out of the nine people who I could see ate that lunch because it was lunch, and it was food, and it looked good.
sentences.zh: 但我能看到的九个人里有六个还是吃了那顿饭，因为那是午餐，是食物，而且看起来不错。

sentences.en: Probably wasn't good if it was airplane food, but, and they ate it.
sentences.zh: 如果是飞机餐的话可能并不好吃，但是，他们还是吃了。

sentences.en: So a lot of what we do is we eat when there's good food around and when the situation is appropriate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很多时候进食，是因为周围有好吃的，而且环境也合适。

sentences.en: Now, if we had left their first lunch and they saw the plate in front of them with pieces of chicken bone,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我们没收走第一份午餐，他们看到面前盘子里还有鸡骨头，

sentences.en: they might have realized that I've just eaten.
sentences.zh: 他们可能就会意识到自己刚吃过饭。

sentences.en: And when we give people, normal people, a second meal in the same way I just described,
sentences.zh: 当我们用同样的方式给普通人提供第二顿饭时，

sentences.en: they don't say, I'm not hungry.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说，我不饿。

sentences.en: They say, I just ate.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我刚吃过。

sentences.en: So it's fascinating because I think what you're saying really is that memory plays a huge role in whether we think we're hungry.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为我认为你真正想表达的是，记忆在我们是否认为自己饥饿这件事上扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: Yes, being hungry is only one reason that we eat.
sentences.zh: 是的，饥饿只是我们进食的原因之一。

sentences.en: So if you go for a full dinner, halfway through that dinner, you're not hungry anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你去吃一顿丰盛的晚餐，吃到一半时，你就不饿了。

sentences.en: But you're still eating the rest of the meal.
sentences.zh: 但你还是会继续吃剩下的饭菜。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So hunger can't institute meals.
sentences.zh: 所以饥饿感并不能决定正餐的开始。

sentences.en: The lack of it will probably discourage you from eating more.
sentences.zh: 没有饥饿感可能会让你不想再多吃。

sentences.en: But there are other things that influence you too.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他因素也会影响你。

sentences.en: When we come back, one of those things is the role that culture plays in our experience of food.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨文化在我们饮食体验中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: We'll also look at how you can serve more memorable meals.
sentences.zh: 我们还将看看如何才能提供更令人难忘的餐点。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Some time ago, one of our producers attended a dinner for Ramadan, an iftar, at an apartment in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我们的一位制片人参加了华盛顿特区一间公寓里举办的斋月开斋饭。

sentences.en: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and commemorates the first revelation of the Koran to the Prophet Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 斋月是伊斯兰历的第九个月，旨在纪念《古兰经》首次向先知穆罕默德显现。

sentences.en: Food plays an important role during Ramadan.
sentences.zh: 食物在斋月期间扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: For 30 days, Muslims like Esma al-Barudi fast from sunrise to sunset as a way to practice self-discipline and to reflect on their connection to their faith.
sentences.zh: 在30天里，像埃斯玛·阿尔-巴鲁迪这样的穆斯林从日出到日落禁食，以此来锻炼自律并反思他们与信仰之间的联系。

sentences.en: So not being able to eat all day and then coming and having that meal makes you grateful for what you have.
sentences.zh: 所以，整天不能吃东西，然后等到开斋时享用那顿饭，会让你对所拥有的一切心存感激。

sentences.en: By deliberately going without food, Tasneem al-Qaik says hunger can make people mindful about the role that food plays in their lives.
sentences.zh: 塔斯尼姆·阿尔-凯克说，通过刻意不进食，饥饿感能让人意识到食物在他们生活中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: The Prophet, he narrated a saying that you should fill your stomach with three things.
sentences.zh: 先知曾讲述过一句格言，说你应该把胃分成三部分来填满。

sentences.en: One-third for food, one-third for drink, and one-third for air.
sentences.zh: 三分之一装食物，三分之一装水，三分之一留给空气。

sentences.en: And so I'm always thinking about that, especially after a long day of fasting,
sentences.zh: 所以我总是记着这一点，特别是在漫长的禁食一天之后，

sentences.en: because it's a natural instinct to just put three-thirds full of food.
sentences.zh: 因为人的本能就是想把胃塞得满满当当的。

sentences.en: And I'm keeping that in mind and constantly reminding myself to always leave room to properly breathe.
sentences.zh: 我一直记在心里，不断提醒自己要留出空间来顺畅呼吸。

sentences.en: Breaking the fast comes with its own rituals.
sentences.zh: 打破禁食有其独特的仪式。

sentences.en: So it's a really, I think, a communal experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的是一种集体体验。

sentences.en: You break your fast almost every single night with friends and family, and you go to the mosque afterwards.
sentences.zh: 你几乎每天晚上都和朋友家人一起开斋，之后还会去清真寺。

sentences.en: Many Muslims at iftar dinners aren't just breaking a faSt.
sentences.zh: 许多穆斯林在开斋晚宴上不仅仅是为了打破禁食。

sentences.en: They're enacting and reinforcing their sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 他们是在实践并强化自己的身份认同感。

sentences.en: Ramadan illustrates the profound role that food plays in shaping our cultural behavior
sentences.zh: 斋月展示了食物在塑造我们文化行为方面的深远影响，

sentences.en: and how culture, in turn, can shape the way we think of food.
sentences.zh: 以及文化反过来如何塑造我们对食物的看法。

sentences.en: And that's the case for Ahmad Asad.
sentences.zh: 艾哈迈德·阿萨德就是如此。

sentences.en: Food is just like the glue that holds a lot of cultures together.
sentences.zh: 食物就像是把许多文化凝聚在一起的胶水。

sentences.en: You know, when I'm like, I'm looking around the room right now,
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像我现在环顾四周，

sentences.en: and there are people from probably like seven or eight different countries.
sentences.zh: 房间里的人可能来自七八个不同的国家。

sentences.en: So it's one of those things, it's like you appreciate other cultures,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是其中之一，你会欣赏其他文化，

sentences.en: and you appreciate, I think, the oneness of, you know, what we are and what Ramadan stands for as a whole.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你会欣赏我们作为一个整体的统一性，以及斋月所代表的意义。

sentences.en: Psychologist Paul Rasen has spent many decades examining the interplay between food, identity, and culture.
sentences.zh: 心理学家保罗·罗津花了数十年时间研究食物、身份和文化之间的相互作用。

sentences.en: Food is not just nutrition that goes in your mouth or even pleasant sensations that go with it.
sentences.zh: 食物不仅仅是进入你嘴里的营养，甚至也不仅仅是随之而来的愉悦感。

sentences.en: It connects to your whole life, and it's really a very important part of performing your culture and experiencing your culture.
sentences.zh: 它与你的整个人生相连，确实是你践行文化和体验文化非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: When Paul asks people about their favorite meals, they certainly mention eating at great restaurants.
sentences.zh: 当保罗问人们最喜欢的餐点时，他们当然会提到在很棒的餐厅用餐。

sentences.en: But they also talk about meals with friends and family, like the one we just heard about.
sentences.zh: 但他们也会谈论与朋友和家人共进的餐点，就像我们刚才听到的那样。

sentences.en: Here's a very common answer that's very short for a home meal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于家常菜非常普遍且简短的回答。

sentences.en: Every Christmas Eve, my Italian grandfather and Greek grandmother would cook a meal
sentences.zh: 每个平安夜，我的意大利爷爷和希腊奶奶都会做一顿饭，

sentences.en: consisting of creamy carbonara with bacon pieces throughout, homemade spinach pie, and sausage.
sentences.zh: 包括满是培根碎的奶油培根面、自制菠菜派和香肠。

sentences.en: It was always amazing.
sentences.zh: 总是棒极了。

sentences.en: And it's connected, of course, to the pleasure of family, not just to the pleasure of food.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与家庭的快乐相连，而不仅仅是食物带来的快乐。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very social.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常有社交意义。

sentences.en: Another one.
sentences.zh: 再来一个。

sentences.en: The best meal I have ever had in my life was when I got out of jail.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子吃过最好的一顿饭是我出狱的时候。

sentences.en: Having been in jail for three years and eating prison food was horrible.
sentences.zh: 在监狱里待了三年，吃着糟糕的监狱伙食。

sentences.en: When I got out, I got a Hardee's Frisco burger combo meal.
sentences.zh: 出来后，我买了一份哈迪斯的弗里斯科汉堡套餐。

sentences.en: That was the best burger and fries I have ever had.
sentences.zh: 那是我吃过最好吃的汉堡和薯条。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's, you know, it's a context.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以你看，这是一种情境。

sentences.en: It's a release from bad eating.
sentences.zh: 这是从糟糕饮食中解脱出来后的感受。

sentences.en: So the contrast is so important there.
sentences.zh: 所以这种对比在那里非常重要。

sentences.en: Contrast and context can also be important when it comes to thinking about an individual meal.
sentences.zh: 在思考个人餐点时，对比和情境也很重要。

sentences.en: Consider the difference between a tapas-style meal and a meal that's built around one large entree.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下塔帕斯风格的餐点和以一道大主菜为核心的餐点之间的区别。

sentences.en: In both cases, you can fill up your stomach.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，你都能填饱肚子。

sentences.en: But it turns out these have very different effects on your brain.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，它们对大脑的影响截然不同。

sentences.en: As social scientists have found, most of us find it difficult to tell the difference between the 10th bite and the 11th bite of the very same food.
sentences.zh: 正如社会科学家发现的那样，我们大多数人很难分辨出同一种食物的第10口和第11口有什么区别。

sentences.en: There's a whole line of modern decision research, most associated with Daniel Kahneman, who got a Nobel Prize for it, and Amos Tversky,
sentences.zh: 现代决策研究中有一整个流派，主要与获得诺贝尔奖的丹尼尔·卡尼曼和阿莫斯·特沃斯基有关，

sentences.en: showing that, you know, people are not so rational as you might expect them to be.
sentences.zh: 他们表明，你知道，人们并不像你预期的那样理性。

sentences.en: And one of the features of it is called duration neglect, which is people don't remember how long an experience is.
sentences.zh: 其中一个特征被称为“持续时间忽视”，即人们记不住一段经历持续了多久。

sentences.en: They just remember the experience.
sentences.zh: 他们只记得这段经历本身。

sentences.en: So if you had a pain for 12 hours or a pain for one hour, two weeks later, what you remember is the experience of the pain, not how long it was.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你忍受了12小时的痛苦或1小时的痛苦，两周后，你记住的是痛苦的经历，而不是它持续了多久。

sentences.en: So this applied to food means that if you have the same food, a lot of the same food,
sentences.zh: 因此，这应用到食物上意味着，如果你吃同样的食物，吃很多同样的食物，

sentences.en: it won't produce a very different memory from having a little of that same food because it's the memory of eating the food.
sentences.zh: 它不会产生与吃少量同样食物截然不同的记忆，因为这是关于吃这种食物的记忆。

sentences.en: So this raises a very important question that Kahneman originally brought up, which is the distinction between your experience and your memory for the experience.
sentences.zh: 这提出了一个卡尼曼最初提出的非常重要的问题，即你的体验与你对体验的记忆之间的区别。

sentences.en: Kahneman and others have shown, we've done some work on this too, that the ending of an experience is particularly important.
sentences.zh: 卡尼曼和其他人已经证明，我们也做过这方面的研究，体验的结尾部分尤为重要。

sentences.en: So when you remember something, you're more likely to remember the end of it.
sentences.zh: 所以当你回忆某件事时，你更有可能记住它的结尾。

sentences.en: And also, by the way, to some extent, more likely to remember the beginning of it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，在某种程度上，也更有可能记住它的开头。

sentences.en: And that would mean if you want to produce the best memory for food, you should put the best foods at the beginning and the end.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你想留下关于食物最好的记忆，你应该把最好的食物放在开头和结尾。

sentences.en: Whereas most people think the entree is the best, which is in the middle and is the least remembered.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人认为主菜是最好的，但它处于中间位置，也是最容易被遗忘的。

sentences.en: We had Danny Kahneman on Hidden Brain recently.
sentences.zh: 我们最近在《隐藏的大脑》节目中请到了丹尼·卡尼曼。

sentences.en: And, of course, he talked about the peak-end rule and also about the difference between the experiencing self and the remembering self.
sentences.zh: 当然，他谈到了“峰终定律”，以及体验自我和记忆自我之间的区别。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And one of the implications of this, as you point out, this difference between experiencing a meal and remembering a meal,
sentences.zh: 正如你指出的那样，体验一顿饭和记住一顿饭之间的这种区别，其含义之一是，

sentences.en: is it points to the difference between people who go to restaurants and order their favorite dish every time
sentences.zh: 它指出了那些去餐厅每次都点自己最爱菜肴的人，

sentences.en: and people who go to a restaurant and order a new dish every time.
sentences.zh: 与那些去餐厅每次都点新菜的人之间的区别。

sentences.en: How are these two strategies essentially catering to two different psychological impulses?
sentences.zh: 这两种策略本质上是如何迎合两种不同的心理冲动的？

sentences.en: Well, that's an issue that we have looked at, and it's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我们研究过的一个问题，答案很明确。

sentences.en: If you're going to order your favorite food, and you know you're going to order that before you go to the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 如果你打算点你最喜欢的食物，而且你在去餐厅之前就知道你要点那个，

sentences.en: there are actually three aspects.
sentences.zh: 实际上有三个方面。

sentences.en: There's your anticipation.
sentences.zh: 你的期待。

sentences.en: This comes from Kahneman.
sentences.zh: 这来自卡尼曼的理论。

sentences.en: The anticipation, the experience, and the memory.
sentences.zh: 期待、体验和记忆。

sentences.en: Your anticipation of a meal is going to be higher if you order your favorite food
sentences.zh: 如果你点的是你最喜欢的食物，你对这顿饭的期待会更高，

sentences.en: because you know you're going to have something great, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你知道你会吃到很棒的东西，对吧？
